title: 2015 HMMT November Guts Problem 27
statement: Let \(A B C D\) be a quadrilateral with \(A=(3,4), B=(9,-40), C=(-5,-12), D=(-7,24)\). Let \(P\) be a point in the plane (not necessarily inside the quadrilateral). Find the minimum possible value of \(A P+B P+C P+D P\).

solutions.text:
Answer: \(16 \sqrt{17}+8 \sqrt{5}\)
By the triangle inequality, \(A P+C P \geq A C\) and \(B P+D P \geq B D\). So \(P\) should be on \(A C\) and \(B D\); i.e. it should be the intersection of the two diagonals. Then \(A P+B P+C P+D P=A C+B D\), which is easily computed to be \(16 \sqrt{17}+8 \sqrt{5}\) by the Pythagorean theorem.
Note that we require the intersection of the diagonals to actually exist for this proof to work, but \(A B C D\) is convex and this is not an issue.
